newsitem.title: USA: Murphy says downstream stronger in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Murphy says downstream stronger in Q1.

text.p: Murphy Oil net income for the first quarter of 1997 rose to $30.6 million, $0.68 a share, from $20.3 million, or $0.45 a share, a year ago, boosted by crude oil and natural gas prices and a turnround in refining and marketing.

"An eight percent increase in U.S. natural gas sales and higher crude oil sales prices worldwide were significant contributors to our exploration and production operations, which earned $25 million in the current quarter compared to $24.4 million a year ago," chief executive Claiborne Deming said in a statement with earnings on Wednesday.

Refining, marketing and transportation in the U.S. earned $5.7 million compared to a loss of $2.7 million a year ago, although this quarter includes a $4.1 million after-tax benefit related to crude oil swap agreements.
Worldwide downstream operations earned $7.8 million in the current quarter compared to a loss of $1.9 million a year ago.
"Margins in our U.S. downstream operations rebounded sharply in the final two months of the quarter, and continued to be strong early in the second quarter," said Deming.
Refinery crude runs were 151,610 barrels a day compared to 139,716 in the first quarter of 1996. Refined product sales were 159,667 barrels a day, up from 148,335 a year ago.

Operations in the UK earned $0.4 million compared with a $0.2 million loss in the first quarter of 1996. Earnings from purchasing, transporting, and reselling crude oil in Canada were $1.7 million in the current quarter compared to $1.0 million loss in the first quarter of 1996.
The company's crude oil and condensate sales prices rose 20 percent to an average $21.81 a barrel in the U.S. and four percent to $20.49 in the UK.
In Canada, sales prices rose 14 percent to an average $19.98 a barrel for light oil and 17 percent to $13.17 for heavy oil.
The average sales price for synthetic oil in Canada rose 19 percent to $22.02 a barrel and in Ecuador synthetic fell five percent to $13.61 a barrel, down five percent.
Total crude oil and gas liquids production averaged 55,078 barrels a day compared to 54,909 in the first quarter of 1996.
U.S. production declined 23 percent due to the sale of onshore producing properties in the third quarter of 1996.
